lemonde.title: Paul et Denise Poiret, splendeurs et misères d’un couple d’avant-garde

zeit.title: Unterhalt: Wie Mütter dafür bestraft werden sollen, dass Väter nicht zahlen
zeit.description: Weil viele Alleinerziehende keinen Unterhalt bekommen, springt der Staat ein. Nun aber soll das eingeschränkt werden – zulasten der Ärmsten. Dabei ginge es anders.

Fußballweltmeisterschaft: Deutscher Schiedsrichter Felix Zwayer reist vorzeitig von WM ab
zeit.description: Der Einsatz des Schiedsrichters Felix Zwayer bei der WM ist nach zwei Spielen beendet. Videoschiedsrichter Bastian Dankert kann sich noch Hoffnungen aufs Finale machen.

france24fr.title: Ebola en RDC : les employés d'un centre de traitement en grève à Rwampara
france24fr.description: En RDC, l’épidémie d’Ebola continue de faire des ravages. Plus de 700 décès ont été enregistrés pour près de 2 000 cas. La situation se complique avec la grève d’une partie du personnel soignant à Rwampara, qui dénonce plusieurs semaines d’impayés.

france24fr.title: France - Espagne en direct : Tchouaméni de retour, Pedri sur le banc, les compos sont là
france24fr.description: La France affronte mardi l'Espagne en demi-finale de la Coupe du monde, à Dallas (Texas, États-Unis). Un choc au sommet pour une place en finale entre les Bleus de Mbappé et la Roja de Lamine Yamal. Suivez la rencontre en direct grâce à notre live commenté.

france24fr.title: Incendie de la forêt de Fontainebleau : "On reste actifs pour ne pas pleurer"
france24fr.description: Alors que plus de 8 % de la surface de la forêt de Fontainebleau ont déjà été consumés dans le pire incendie qu’ait connu la région parisienne depuis 1921, plusieurs habitants des communes avoisinantes, amoureux du lieu, ont accepté de témoigner pour France 24.

france24fr.title: De Kinshasa au Mondial, les coulisses d'une création made in Congo pour les Léopards
france24fr.description: Portée par les Léopards à leur arrivée aux États-Unis pour la Coupe du monde 2026, cette veste est le fruit d'un savoir-faire 100 % congolais. Notre reportage vous emmène dans les coulisses de la maison de couture dirigée par Charlotte Kambeya, où a été confectionnée cette création imaginée par le styliste Alvin J Mak, entièrement réalisée à Kinshasa.

france24fr.title: Tour de France : au Lioran, Tadej Pogacar s'offre une troisième victoire d'étape
france24fr.description: Le Slovène Tadej Pogacar a remporté mardi la 10e étape du Tour de France, au Lorian, dans le Massif central. Une troisième victoire d'étape qui lui permet de conserver son maillot jaune et de creuser l'écart avec Jonas Vingegaard et Remco Evenepoel au classement général.

france24fr.title: Destination Brésil : 9 millions d'étrangers ont afflués l’an dernier, un record
france24fr.description: Le tour du monde de l'été de France 24 nous emmène au Brésil, destination phare où 9 millions d'étrangers ont afflués l’an dernier, un record ! Ce choix, les Brésiliens eux-mêmes le comprennent bien car ils voyagent principalement à l’intérieur de leur pays : Rio de Janeiro, Salvador, le Nordeste… 63% des Brésiliens déclarent que s’ils reçoivent des vacances gratuites, ils choisissent de partir au Brésil. Décryptage avec notre correspondante au Brésil, Marine Resse.

france24fr.title: "Les supporters espagnols très impatients" pour cette demi-finale France-Espagne
france24fr.description: La France et son attaque étincelante à la poursuite d'une troisième finale consécutive face à l'Espagne de Lamine Yamal : comme attendu, les deux équipes les plus impressionnantes du Mondial 2026 se retrouvent dans une demi-finale aux allures d'immense choc.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : France-Espagne, premier choc du dernier carré

france24fr.title: L'Iran rapporte des frappes américaines dans la région proche de l'Irak et du Koweït
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a estimé qu'un accord était encore "possible" avec l'Iran, malgré le lancement de nouvelles frappes américaines et le rétablissement du blocus des ports iraniens. Ces frappes américaines ont visé mardi après-midi le sud-ouest de l'Iran, dans une zone pétrolifère proche de l'Irak et du Koweït, ont rapporté les autorités locales.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Incendies en forêt de Fontainebleau : six personnes en garde à vue, dont un pompier volontaire qui a reconnu les faits
Ces acteurs étrangers qui surfent sur les crises climatiques pour diffuser de la désinformation
france24fr.description: Alors que les événements météorologiques extrêmes se multiplient, les crises climatiques peuvent être instrumentalisées par des acteurs étrangers. Un rapport de l'Iris met en garde : la désinformation climatique est devenue un véritable "outil de déstabilisation".

france24fr.title: Soudan : le général Hemedti, chef des FSR condamné à mort par contumace
france24fr.description: Au Soudan, la justice a condamné à mort par contumace le chef des Forces de soutien rapide, le général Hemedti. Il est reconnu coupable de crimes de guerre, crimes contre l’humanité et génocide, notamment au Darfour occidental.

france24fr.title: Dix ans après l'attentat de Nice : "c'est le rôle de l'Etat d'honorer nos morts"
france24fr.description: Dix ans après l'attentat qui a fait 86 morts et plus de 400 blessés le 14 juillet 2016 sur la Promenade des Anglais, Nice rend hommage aux victimes en présence d'Emmanuel Macron, une commémoration qui coïncide avec la demi-finale des Bleus au Mondial, où une minute de silence sera observée. Pour Céline Viale, qui a perdu sa mère en 2016, "c'est le rôle de l'Etat d'honorer nos morts".

france24fr.title: Epidémie d'Ebola en RD Congo : les employés d'un centre de santé en grève
france24fr.description: L'ampleur de l'épidémie d'Ebola en RD Congo pourrait dépasser "de deux à quatre fois" les estimations officielles, a indiqué mardi l'Organisation mondiale de la santé. En RD Congo, des professionnels de la santé, pas payés depuis 45 jours, sont en grève.

france24fr.title: Dix ans attentat de Nice : la menace terroriste polymorphe
france24fr.description: Dix ans après l'attentat qui a fait 86 morts et plus de 400 blessés le 14 juillet 2016 sur la Promenade des Anglais, Nice rend hommage aux victimes en présence d'Emmanuel Macron. Il y a dix ans, le Tunisien Mohamed Lahouaiej-Bouhlel a provoqué un carnage en fonçant sur près de deux kilomètres au volant d'un camion de 19 tonnes dans la foule qui venait d'assister au feu d'artifice, avant d'être abattu par la police.

france24fr.title: Comment un groupe terroriste comme Boko Haram utilise l’intelligence artificielle
france24fr.description: Pour la première fois, un rapport publié vendredi par l’université de Cambridge compile des témoignages d’anciens membres du mouvement terroriste Boko Haram au Nigeria qui expliquent comment l'organisation utilise l’IA depuis 2023. Un constat qui s’applique probablement à d’autres groupes terroristes, assurent les experts interrogés.

france24fr.title: Forêt de Fontainebleau : "le feu n'est pas encore fixé mais la situation s'améliore"
france24fr.description: Les deux incendies qui ravagent la forêt de Fontainebleau, en région parisienne, ont parcouru un peu plus de 2 000 hectares, a annoncé mardi à la mi-journée le préfet du département, qui a donné aux plus de 800 pompiers mobilisés "l'objectif" de "fixer" les feux d'ici à la fin de la journée. Les Canadair écope l'eau de la Seine pour verser sur ces feux. "Le feu n'est pas encore fixé mais la situation s'améliore" a confié un pompier sur place à notre reporter Catherine Norris Trent.

france24fr.title: 14-Juillet en France : retour sur le dernier défilé d'Emmanuel Macron
france24fr.description: Emmanuel Macron préside mardi pour la dernière fois le traditionnel défilé militaire du 14-Juillet, une édition 2026 voulue "massive" et qui mettra à l'honneur l'Ukraine et ses alliés, essentiellement européens.

spiegel.title: Spanien: Bruder von Pedro Sánchez wegen Vetternwirtschaft verurteilt
spiegel.description: Ein Gericht hat den Bruder von Spaniens Ministerpräsident Sánchez wegen Amtsmissbrauchs verurteilt. Das Urteil erhöht den Druck auf den Regierungschef, dessen Umfeld seit Monaten von Korruptionsaffären erschüttert wird.

spiegel.title: Jörg Thadeusz: Neuer Chef der Verlagspreis-Jury verteidigt erst einmal Kulturstaatsminister Weimer
spiegel.description: Der Moderator und Schriftsteller Jörg Thadeusz übernimmt den Juryvorsitz für den Deutschen Verlagspreis. Hier verteidigt er Kulturstaatsminister Weimer und dessen umstrittene Änderung des Vergabeverfahrens.

spiegel.title: München: Dominik Krause verkündet Maßnahmen wegen Wasserknappheit
spiegel.description: Die bayerische Landeshauptstadt muss ihre Wasserreserven sichern. Deshalb ruft Oberbürgermeister Krause erneut zum Sparen auf. Und verkündet mehrere Maßnahmen, die auch die Bürger treffen.

spiegel.title: Diagnose Multiple Sklerose: Die Krankheit der tausend Gesichter - SPIEGEL TV für Arte Re
spiegel.description: Tremor, Lähmung, Sprachverlust: All das können Symptome der Autoimmunerkrankung MS sein. »Die Krankheit ist ein Biest«, sagt Emily Wittmann. Wie schafft die junge Mutter ihren Alltag? Eine »Arte Re:«-Reportage von SPIEGEL TV.

spiegel.title: Kolonien auf dem Mars: Was die US-Weltraumträume mit amerikanischer Geschichte zu tun haben
spiegel.description: Einst war der Wilde Westen der Raum, in dem sich Amerikaner beweisen und als Helden zeigen konnten. Unternehmer wie Elon Musk übertragen diese uralten Ideen auf neues Terrain: den Weltraum.

spiegel.title: Ukraine-Krieg: Russland könnte die Stadt Kostjantyniwka einnehmen - aber zu welchem Preis?

spiegel.description: Auch am 14. Juli macht Tadej Pogačar die Tour de France zu seiner Veranstaltung. Der Slowene attackiert am letzten Berg im Zentralmassiv. Folgen kann ihm keiner.

spiegel.description: Die französische Nationalmannschaft um Kylian Mbappé wurde bei dieser WM wiederholt rassistisch beleidigt. Äußerungen des früheren spanischen Regierungschefs Rajoy überschatten nun das Halbfinale.

spiegel.description: Weil der Markt durch Labordiamanten belastet ist, zieht der Konzern De Beers Konsequenzen: Die Venetia-Mine in Südafrika soll vorübergehend ihren Betrieb einstellen. Betroffen sind rund 4400 Arbeiter.

spiegel.description: Nach dem WM-Aus der Nationalelf bestimmen Männer die Diskussion über die Zukunft des deutschen Fußballs. Die TV-Expertinnen Friederike Kromp und Tabea Kemme beweisen: Es würde sich lohnen, andere Wege zu gehen.

spiegel.description: Er tönte zuletzt, die USA seien der »Hüter der Straße von Hormus«. Dafür wollte Donald Trump Gebühren in Höhe von 20 Prozent auf jede beförderte Fracht erheben. Nun hat der US-Präsident wieder eine andere Idee.

spiegel.description: Vor etwa 1200 Jahren stellte ein Gelehrter der Maya komplexe Berechnungen an. Seinen Namen haben Forschende nun Mikrotexten in einer Kammer der Ruinenstadt Xultún zugeordnet.

spiegel.description: Jahrelang hat Bill Gates’ Stiftung Großspenden von Warren Buffett erhalten. Damit ist vorerst Schluss. Der 95-Jährige will erst wieder mit dem Microsoft-Mitgründer sprechen, wenn es Klarheit über dessen Epstein-Kontakte gebe.

spiegel.description: Ebola breitet sich im Kongo häufig über unbekannte Wege aus, berichtet die Weltgesundheitsorganisation. Viele Infizierte werden demnach nicht erfasst und können dann auch nicht von Ärzten behandelt werden.

nzz.title: Erstmals nehmen an der grossen Militärparade in Paris ukrainische Soldaten teil – die Bilder
nzz.description: Die letzte Militärparade unter Macron steht im Zeichen der europäischen Verteidigungsbereitschaft. Zum ersten Mal waren ukrainische Soldaten Teil der Feierlichkeiten.

nzz.title: Schüsse in Regensdorf: Medien berichten von Drogen- und Alkoholproblemen des Täters
nzz.description: Am frühen Dienstagmorgen meldeten Anwohner Schüsse aus einem Wohnhaus. Stunden später stellte sich der Schütze der Polizei. Unter Nachbarn war der Mann offenbar kein Unbekannter.

nzz.title: Explosion im Tessin: Polizei vermutet Sprengsatzfalle für die Einsatzkräfte
nzz.description: Bei einem Einsatz der Sondereinheit in Leontica wurden drei Polizisten verletzt. Die Tessiner Kantonspolizei nimmt an, dass der mutmassliche Täter es auf das Sonderkommando der Polizei abgesehen hatte.

nzz.title: Macrons letzte Militärparade ist ein Signal an Moskau und Washington
nzz.description: Frankreich inszenierte seine bislang grösste Militärparade am 14. Juli als Botschaft der Stärke. Ehrengast war der ukrainische Präsident Selenski. Macron machte daraus auch eine Bilanz seiner Amtszeit.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Wirtschaft: Siemens Energy spart Hunderte Millionen und streicht deshalb Siemens aus dem Namen
LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Berichte über Angriffe auf Ukrainer in Polen mehren sich +++ Ukraine greift eine russische Raffinerie in der Nähe des Uralgebirges an
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Europa handelt viel zu spät: Die Ukraine braucht jetzt eine bessere Raketenabwehr, nicht erst in einigen Jahren
nzz.description: Russlands Raketen töten fast täglich Menschen. Umso schwerer wiegt das Versagen des Westens: Statt Soforthilfe gegen den Terror des Kremls bietet er den Ukrainern nur Versprechungen für die Zukunft.

nzz.title: Mehrere Tote nach Gebäudebrand in Brüssel
nzz.description: Ein Gebäude in der Innenstadt Brüssels wird umgebaut, Hunderte Arbeiter sind vor Ort. Dann bricht ein Feuer aus. Mehrere Personen kommen ums Leben.

nzz.title: Milliarden für Helsing: Noch nie hat ein deutsches Startup so viel Geld auf einmal eingesammelt
nzz.description: Während in der Rüstungsbranche Konzerne wie Rheinmetall an der Börse schwächeln, feiern Startups Erfolge. So wie Helsing: Bei der Münchner Firma haben gerade die US-Finanzriesen JP Morgan und Goldman Sachs investiert.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Fünf Jahre nach der Ahrtal-Flut: Bilder einer Katastrophe
nzz.description: Das Hochwasser in der Nacht vom 14. auf den 15. Juli 2021 in Rheinland-Pfalz und Nordrhein-Westfalen war eine der verheerendsten Naturkatastrophen in der jüngeren deutschen Geschichte.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Hitze in Europa: München verbietet Rasenbewässerung und das Füllen von Pools +++ Schweiz erwartet Abkühlung mit Gewittern
nzz.description: Wo ist es derzeit besonders heiss? Und welche sind die Auswirkungen auf die Menschen und die Umwelt? Hier sind die neuesten Meldungen zu Hitzerekorden, Dürren und Bränden in Europa zu finden.

nzz.title: VIDEO - 5 Jahre nach der verheerenden Flut in Ahrweiler – eine Video-Rekonstruktion des Hochwassers
nzz.description: Beim Hochwasser im Juli 2021 verlieren im Landkreis Ahrweiler mehr als 130 Menschen ihr Leben. Die Video-Rekonstruktion zeigt, warum die Flut genau dort so verheerend war.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Oliver Blume hat für die Volkswagen-Sanierung zwei radikale Optionen – zur Rettung des Konzerns muss er sie erwägen
nzz.description: Das Überleben von Europas grösstem Autobauer ist in Gefahr. Das Gesundschrumpfen funktioniert nicht ohne die Anpassung der Kosten in Deutschland. Doch das Bollwerk Wolfsburg ist schwer zu schleifen.

nzz.title: «Grösser als die industrielle Revolution»: 200 Ökonomen und Tech-Bosse warnen vor KI. Selbst frühere Skeptiker sind nun alarmiert
nzz.description: Führende Wissenschafter äussern sich besorgt über die möglichen wirtschaftlichen Folgen der künstlichen Intelligenz. Bemerkenswert ist, wer den Aufruf unterschrieben hat – und was die Daten zum Arbeitsmarkt tatsächlich zeigen.

nzz.title: Grossbrand im Wald von Fontainebleau: zwei Verdächtige wegen Brandstiftung festgenommen
nzz.description: Frankreich kämpft seit Jahren gegen schwere Waldbrände im Sommer. Aber vor allem im Süden des Landes. Dass nun aber ausgerechnet vor den Toren von Paris die Flammen lodern, ist eine Zäsur.

observador.title: Jornalistas alertam para desafios ao jornalismo parlamentar
observador.description: Um livro com 20 autores e jornalistas de várias gerações reflete sobre 50 anos desta especialidade. É apresentado esta quarta-feira na Assembleia da República.

observador.title: Sul-coreanos levaram bandeira da Palestina para o Mundial?
observador.description: Vídeo em que se vê adeptos sul-coreanos num estádio mostraria bandeiras da Palestina durante jogo do Mundial de 2026 no México. Gesto de solidariedade terá mesmo acontecido?

observador.title: Laporte nasceu em França, mas joga por Espanha
observador.description: O central que fez grande parte da carreira no Athletic de Bilbao trocou palavras tensas com o selecionador Deschamps por não ser convocado. Em 2021, optou por Espanha.

observador.title: Política Externa. PSD diz que Portugal tem de ter uma voz...
observador.description: Ricardo Carvalho (PSD), Pedro Correia (Chega) e Ana Catarina Louro (PS) em debate sobre a política externa do país e sobre a subscrição à declaração conjunta para a reabertura do Estreito de Ormuz.

observador.title: PM disse: trabalhadores "queixam-se e só pensam em férias"?
observador.description: Uma imagem falsificada com o grafismo do Diário de Notícias atribui declarações inventadas a Luís Montenegro. A fotografia usada é real, mas é de 2024.

observador.title: Abusos sexuais. Igreja quer colaborar com sociedade civil
observador.description: O porta-voz da Conferência Episcopal Portuguesa contestou o silêncio do Estado nos apoios às vítimas de abusos sexuais na Igreja Católica. As vítimas vão receber entre 9 mil e 45 mil euros.

observador.title: Homem morre em despiste de um motociclo em Tondela
observador.description: O acidente ocorreu esta terça-feira no centro da localidade. GNR, INEM e Bombeiros de Vale de Besteiros responderam à ocorrência com 17 operacionais.

observador.title: IL sem apoio para adiar debate do Estado da Nação
observador.description: Aguiar-Branco rejeitou pedido da IL para passar Estado da Nação para depois do debate de urgência com o ministro da Educação sobre exames. Liberais ainda tentam, mas PS e Chega não mostram interesse.

observador.title: Como o Volta criou uma autêntica "caça ao lixo" em Lisboa
observador.description: Sistema de Depósito e Reembolso pretendia promover a redução de lixo nos espaços públicos. Contudo, terá tido o efeito contrário e as autarquias queixam-se do aumento de resíduos espalhados no chão.

observador.title: "A Odisseia”: Christopher Nolan retalha e destrata Homero
observador.description: Christopher Nolan pegou na "Odisseia" de Homero e filmou uma versão "woke", fatiada, baralhada e deficitária de empolgamento e de maravilhoso do poema épico. Eurico de Barros dá-lhe uma estrela.

observador.title: E. Jean Carroll recebeu indemnização de 5,6 milhões de Trump
observador.description: Três anos após o júri responsabilizar o Presidente norte-americano por abuso sexual e difamação, E. Jean Carroll recebeu a indemnização. Escritora quer usar o dinheiro para financiar a reforma.

observador.title: Soldados israelitas gravaram-se a destruir igreja no Líbano?
observador.description: Depois do escândalo causado por atos de vandalismo e desrespeito a estátuas cristãs no Líbano, começou a circular um vídeo onde dois militares israelitas parecem destruir uma igreja nesse mesmo país.

observador.title: 412 incidentes e mais de 200 feridos em protestos anti-ICE
observador.description: Estudo documenta violência em cidades como LA, Chicago e Minneapolis. Uso indevido de armas de controlo pelas autoridades causou cegueira, traumatismo e fraturas. 43% dos alvos foram jornalistas.

observador.title: 18h. Ventura quer falar com Seguro sobre Luís Montenegro
observador.description: Líder do Chega é recebido amanhã em Belém pelo Presidente da República. Ainda neste jornal, ministra do ambiente culpa autarquia de Almada e o SMAS pela crise no abastecimento de água no concelho.

observador.title: Nome de Trump foi retirado do Kennedy Center?
observador.description: Apesar de a decisão judicial ser real, o vídeo viral é falso. Até 1 de junho, o nome permanecia na fachada. A remoção só aconteceu na madrugada de 13 de junho.

observador.title: Câmara do Porto estuda locais para alargar videovigilância
observador.description: Câmara do Porto diz que "problema da segurança continua a ser um desafio para a cidade, essencialmente associado ao problema da droga" e refere que as câmaras de videovigilância podem ser dissuasoras.

observador.title: PM cabo-verdiano acusado de crimes enquanto autarca
observador.description: Francisco Carvalho responde por corrupção, peculato, abuso de poder e falsificação, entre outros. Crimes terão sido praticados entre 2020 e 2026 na Câmara de Praia.

observador.title: Reforma laboral. Ministra vai "devolver palavra" a parceiros
observador.description: Levantando a ponta do véu para a reunião da concertação social desta quarta-feira, Palma Ramalho diz querer ouvir parceiros sobre novo caminho da reforma laboral. Salário mínimo para 2027 em aberto.

elpais.title: Condenado David Sánchez, hermano del presidente del Gobierno, a nueve años de inhabilitación por un delito de prevaricación
elpais.description: La Audiencia de Badajoz descarta el tráfico de influencias e impone 18 años de inhabilitación al exlíder del PSOE extremeño Miguel Ángel Gallardo

elpais.title: Las “dudas” del tribunal sobre la contratación de David Sánchez: sin tráfico de influencias ni presiones acreditadas
elpais.description: La sentencia de la Audiencia de Badajoz considera que no se ha probado quién está detrás de la creación y adjudicación de la plaza al hermano del presidente

elpais.title: Claves de una sentencia inédita: un trabajo “a medida” sin prueba de presiones externas
elpais.description: Los tres magistrados firman un fallo unánime donde concluyen que el puesto que se dio a David Sánchez no era “urgente” ni necesario, sino que solo obedeció a su “interés particular”

elpais.title: El Gobierno denuncia que lo pretenden “derribar” ante “la incapacidad de hacerlo por las urnas” tras la condena al hermano de Sánchez
elpais.description: Rebeca Torró atribuye la sentencia a “una estrategia para desgastar” al Ejecutivo “por cualquier medio” y Patxi López califica el fallo de “cacería” contra el PSOE y el presidente

elpais.title: El PP considera que la sentencia al hermano de Sánchez “haría caer a un Gobierno” en cualquier otro país
elpais.description: “Que nadie esté por encima de la ley, sea familia de quien sea, habla bien de nuestro Estado de derecho”, apunta Feijóo

elpais.title: Última hora de la actualidad política, en directo | Rufián, sobre la condena a David Sánchez: “Es una sobrada importante (…) Luego viene Begoña Gómez”
elpais.description: Figaredo (Vox): “Esta sentencia demuestra que estos tipos son unos chorizos” | Óscar Puente afirma que se pretende “derribar” al Gobierno “ante la incapacidad de hacerlo por las urnas” | Ester Muñoz (PP): “Hoy es un día histórico; en cualquier país haría caer a un Gobierno”

elpais.title: David Sánchez, el hijo de Magdalena y Pedro
elpais.description: Del hermano de Sánchez se han dicho muchas cosas, pero puede que a él le chirríe que se diga que su puesto de coordinador fue un traje a medida, cuando se lo acusa de prevaricación sin pruebas

elpais.title: Francia - España: Mundial 2026, en directo | Pedri es suplente y De la Fuente repite el once con el que ganó a Bélgica
elpais.description: Deschamps introduce dos cambios en la alineación titular: entran Tchouameni por Koné y Barcola por Doué | El miércoles, otra semifinal de alto voltaje: Inglaterra - Argentina

elpais.title: Los datos de España y Francia: ¿quién ha jugado mejor en el Mundial?
elpais.description: Analizamos los seis partidos que los llevan a semifinales

elpais.title: El Mbappé más explosivo y solidario se mide a la defensa menos goleada: “Es una misión especial”
elpais.description: Francia juega para los desmarques en corto de su capitán, también más implicado en la presión

elpais.title: ¿Qué selecciones han sido las mejores en el Mundial? Consulte sus datos partido a partido
elpais.description: Un interactivo de EL PAÍS con métricas de la FIFA y Driblab: goles esperados, red de pases, mejores jugadores, distancia recorrida y mucho más

elpais.title: Mundial 2026: Programa ‘Fútbol chapa’ | Previa de la semifinal entre España y Francia
elpais.description: El análisis y la última hora del duelo por un puesto en la final, en directo a partir de las 15.00

elpais.title: La UE y el Reino Unido firman el acuerdo histórico que acaba con la verja de Gibraltar
elpais.description: El pacto es el último de los grandes asuntos pendientes del Brexit

elpais.title: Al menos cinco muertos en un incendio en el corazón de Bruselas
elpais.description: El fuego atrapó a varios trabajadores en los ascensores de un edificio en obras

elpais.title: Estados Unidos e Irán vuelven a la guerra abierta tras una semana de enfrentamientos en Ormuz
elpais.description: Los ataques a petroleros matan a un marinero y provocan ocho heridos. Trump da marcha atrás en su intención de cobrar por el uso del estrecho a los barcos extranjeros

elpais.title: Varios congresistas piden a Trump que levante las sanciones a Venezuela para gestionar la catástrofe del terremoto
elpais.description: 14 representantes demócratas envían una carta junto a 17 ONG en la que advierten de que las restricciones financieras obstaculizan las labores de socorro y amenazan la recuperación del país

elpais.title: Macron celebra su último 14 de julio con una exhibición del rearme europeo
elpais.description: Los militares franceses desfilaron junto a tropas de los países de la coalición de voluntarios que apoya a Ucrania para lanzar un mensaje de unidad y poderío frente a Rusia

elpais.title: ¿Cuántas personas han muerto por disparos de agentes migratorios en medio de la ofensiva de Trump?
elpais.description: Elementos del ICE y la Patrulla Fronteriza han protagonizado al menos 29 tiroteos desde el regreso del republicano a la Casa Blanca, siendo el caso de Maine el más reciente

nyt.title: Trump Paid $2 Million by South Korean Company Facing Trade Investigation
nyt.description: The payment illustrates the minefield Mr. Trump has created by maintaining personal financial ties with foreign businesses while he is in office.

nyt.title: ‘I Am Frustrated’: Emails Show Blanche’s Role in Trump’s Retribution Campaign
nyt.description: The cooperation of Todd Blanche will be a flashpoint in his confirmation hearing to be attorney general on Wednesday.

nyt.title: Mahmoud Khalil Accuses Trump Officials of Conspiring Against Him
nyt.description: Mr. Khalil will now have to convince a judge that the defendants coordinated to take action against him and other pro-Palestinian activists.

nyt.title: ICE Ordered to Cease Most Vehicle Stops After Fatal Shootings in Maine and Houston
nyt.description: Agents fatally shot a man in Houston and another in coastal Maine, both in their vehicles. The killings were the latest in a string of ICE shootings during President Trump’s second term.

nyt.title: Maine ICE Shooting: What We Know About the Death of Joan Sebastian Guerrero
nyt.description: A federal immigration agent shot and killed a man in a car on Monday morning in Biddeford, Maine. It was the second fatal encounter in a week involving an agent and a person in a vehicle.

nyt.title: ICE Shot Lorenzo Salgado Araujo Through Open Passenger Window in Houston, Witnesses Say
nyt.description: A congresswoman and a lawyer relayed witness accounts that diverge from Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s version of the fatal encounter.

nyt.title: Man in Florida Fatally Hit by Truck While Fleeing ICE, Official Says
nyt.description: Details about what exactly happened at a gas station in St. Augustine before the man was hit were unclear Tuesday.

nyt.title: At 91, He’s Hiking the Appalachian Trail. Again.
nyt.description: Dale “Grey Beard” Sanders once set the record as the oldest person to complete the roughly 2,190-mile trail. Now, he’s back for his title.

nyt.title: E. Jean Carroll Receives $5.6 Million Payment From Trump in Civil Case
nyt.description: A federal jury found President Trump liable for sexually assaulting and defaming Ms. Carroll. He exhausted his appeals last month, prompting a judge to order that the money be paid.

nyt.title: The Strange Phenomenon of ‘Terminal Lucidity’
nyt.description: As they near death, some dementia patients recover mental faculties assumed to be long lost. Researchers want to know why.

nyt.title: Big Banks Smash Earnings Records, but ‘Tectonic’ Risks Loom
nyt.description: The quarterly results reflect the dichotomy between geopolitical uncertainty and the stable American economy.

nyt.title: Inflation Slowed During Pause in War With Iran
nyt.description: The Consumer Price Index fell to a 3.5 percent annual increase in June, and prices marked their biggest drop from a month earlier since 2020.

nyt.title: A Beastie Boy Returns to the Mic, With Some Help
nyt.description: Thanks to an assist from his sons, Mike D is set to release “Thank You,” the first new music from a member of the pioneering rap trio in 15 years.

nyt.title: China Purges Top Official Over Corruption and Sex Charges
nyt.description: Ma Xingrui is the third member of the Politburo to be purged since 2022. He once led the Xinjiang region and was previously head of China’s space program.

nyt.title: T. Rex Fossil Sells for $50.1 Million, Putting the King Back On Top
nyt.description: In a booming fossil market, the T. rex had been dethroned by a stegosaurus. No longer.

nyt.title: 75 Years Later, ‘The Catcher in the Rye’ Remains a Great American Novel
nyt.description: Sure, “Catcher in the Rye” has its detractors. But the influence of its wised-up yet winningly innocent hero keeps it among the Great American Novels.

nyt.title: The Housing Crisis Is Also a Retirement Crisis
nyt.description: A home has stopped being just a place to live — it has also become an asset.

nyt.title: The Ukraine-Russia War Reaches a New Phase
nyt.description: The ground war in Ukraine has stalemated and the crucial fight has shifted to the skies — missiles and interceptors.

npr.title: U.S. to reinstate Hormuz blockade. And, states sue over Paramount-Warner deal
npr.description: The United States plans to reinstate a blockade over the Strait of Hormuz today. And, several states are suing to stop the massive Paramount-Warner Bros. merger.

npr.title: Trump scraps his Hormuz shipping charge idea but presses ahead with an Iran blockade
npr.description: The U.S. military announced it will begin its blockade of Iranian ships over the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, as Iran vowed to assert its own control over the critical international waterway.

npr.title: Death toll from a Bangkok music bar fire rises to 30, dozens remain in hospital
npr.description: More than 70 people were injured, with 24 of them still in critical condition, according to a statement by the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration.

npr.title: Pakistan urges restraint as its Mideast deal unravels
npr.description: Pakistan urges restraint as Iran and the U.S. clash and a memorandum of understanding unravels.

npr.title: People watching the World Cup during work hours is leading to a drop in productivity
npr.description: The global economy may be suffering from lost productivity as people get swept by World Cup fever, a survey shows. This small business owner would know. She's spent most of her days watching matches.

npr.title: The U.S. strikes Iran after Trump announces a renewed blockade and tolls in Hormuz
npr.description: The U.S. and Iran are fighting for control of the Strait of Hormuz, threatening a return to all-out war after agreeing to a ceasefire last month.

npr.title: The U.S.-Iran ceasefire grows more distant. And, Congress faces a consequential week
npr.description: The U.S. and Iran exchanged fire over the weekend amid tensions over the Strait of Hormuz. And, Congress returns from recess facing tight deadlines.

npr.title: Sam Neill, known for 'Jurassic Park' and 'The Piano,' dies at 78, his family says
npr.description: In 2023, Neill disclosed he had been diagnosed with angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma, a rare type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Neill died on Monday in Sydney, according to a statement posted to the actor's social media page.

npr.title: What would it mean for Ukraine if it actually starts producing Patriot missiles?
npr.description: NPR's Don Gonyea speaks with Seth Jones from the Center for Strategic and International Studies about President Trump granting Ukraine permission to produce Patriot missiles.

npr.title: Investigators probe a fire at a music bar in Bangkok that killed at least 27 people
npr.description: By Monday morning, forensic teams were investigating the scene. Officials say many victims were trapped in windowless bathrooms near a rear exit. Investigators are focusing on the ceiling above the performance stage for clues.

republika.title: Piantedosi: “Fermo preventivo esteso ai minorenni”
republika.description: Il consiglio dei ministri ha approvato il ddl sicurezza. Tra le novità, la possibilità di applicare la misura, che viene estesa anche alla polizia locale

republika.title: Migrante picchiato denuncia l’esponente di Futuro Nazionale che lo ha aggredito in strada
republika.description: L’episodio a San Benedetto del Tronto sabato scorso. Giuseppe Barboni aveva preso a pugni l’iracheno postando poi il video sui social. Vannacci: “Sono contro la violenza se non per difesa”

republika.title: I figli di Trump investono miliardi nella difesa proprio mentre gli Usa puntano sulla spesa militare
republika.description: Le società sostenute dai fondi riconducibili a Donald Jr. ed Eric hanno ricevuto almeno 3,2 miliardi di dollari in contratti già assegnati dall'amministrazione federale. La coincidenza ha scatenato le polemiche, ma la Casa Bianca ha respinto ogni accusa: “Decidiamo in base al merito”

republika.title: Meno donne in Parlamento, le trappole nell’emendamento della destra sulle preferenze
republika.description: Le conseguenze della proposta di modifica firmata FdI e Noi moderati con l’ok di Forza Italia e Lega

republika.title: Incendio in un edificio nel centro di Bruxelles: almeno sei morti e alcuni dispersi
republika.description: Il complesso residenziale era stato appena ristrutturato. Le fiamme partite dal secondo piano si sono propagate nel vano ascensore

republika.title: Che cosa è “Pickaxe Mountain”, il sito nucleare iraniano nel mirino di Trump
republika.description: La minaccia del presidente americano ha acceso i riflettori sull’impianto che gli iraniani avrebbero costruito a centinaia di metri sotto una montagna alta circa 1.600 metri. Ma è protetto da una roccia densa ed è così in profondità da poter resistere ai “bunker buster” americani

republika.title: Sondaggi politici, crescono i partiti del centrodestra tranne la Lega sorpassata ancora da Vannacci
republika.description: Il Carroccio è l’unico in calo restando sotto Futuro nazionale. Scendono di poco anche Pd e M5S

republika.title: Al lavoro “a 50 gradi”, la denuncia dei sindacati. Giovedì il picco: bollino rosso in 15 città
republika.description: Più della metà delle città monitorate in allerta. Tra cantieri, autogrill e uffici postali, il caldo estremo mette a nudo le falle nella tutela dei lavoratori e spinge i Comuni a correre ai ripari per gli anziani

republika.title: Rai, Rossi: “Repliche Report sospese per tutelare il brand. Senza Vigilanza scenario non tranquillo”
republika.description: L’amministratore delegato spiega il motivo della sospensione delle puntate estive della trasmissione di Ranucci

republika.title: Legge elettorale, bocciate le preferenze: vincono i franchi tiratori
republika.description: La maggioranza si era compattata sull’emendamento. Il Pd chiede il voto segreto, Schlein: “Il Melonellum è l’unica vera priorità della destra”. L’ultimo appello di Meloni: “Mettere la faccia sullo scrutinio”. Cori dai banchi delle opposizioni: “Elezioni”

republika.title: “L’IA impoverisce l’informazione, pluralismo a rischio. Giganti web paghino gli editori”
republika.description: Giacomo Lasorella, presidente del Garante Agcom, lancia l’allarme. I motori di risposta, e non più di ricerca, forniscono una sintesi già pronta chiavi in mano. Negato l’accesso a una pluralità di fonti

republika.title: Soffocò la madre malata di Alzheimer. Assolta: stress per l’assistenza. “Non riesco a perdonarmi”
republika.description: La Corte d’Assise l’ha riconosciuta incapace di intendere e di volere per il peso dell’accudimento

republika.title: Pedaggi nello Stretto di Hormuz, così Trump smentisce Rubio e Vance
republika.description: Con l’annuncio della richiesta di “rimborsi del 20%” per la protezione delle navi, il presidente Usa ribalta la linea annunciata dai suoi che avevano anche firmato una dichiarazione congiunta sulla libertà di transito. Gli analisti prevedono il raddoppio del costo delle spedizioni di greggio.

republika.title: Parigi, applausi per Zelensky e i soldati ucraini alla parata del 14 luglio
republika.description: Si commemora l’avvio della Rivoluzione francese e si celebra il “risveglio strategico dell’Europa”: rappresentanti di 35 Stati sulla tribuna d’onore. Mattarella ricorda le vittime dell’attentato di Nizza del 14 luglio 2016

republika.title: IA, si passa dalle tariffe fisse a quelle a consumo: per le aziende è un choc, quali soluzioni

phys-org.description: Evidence of the slowing of Charon's spin period (despinning) is recorded in tectonic features on the surface of Pluto's icy moon, according to a modeling study published in Nature Communications. The findings offer insights into the early thermal evolution of Charon and other icy satellites in the outer solar system.

phys-org.title: Magnetic fingerprint of a cosmic explosion detected for the first time
phys-org.description: Astronomers have made a series of landmark observations of one of the universe's most violent events. Using the U.S. National Science Foundation Very Large Array (NSF VLA) radio telescope, which is operated by the U.S. National Science Foundation National Radio Astronomy Observatory (NSF NRAO), the team detected polarized light from a gamma-ray burst (GRB) afterglow for the first time at radio wavelengths.

phys-org.title: New platform uncovers genetic edits that boost plant-derived compound production
phys-org.description: Microorganisms are increasingly being engineered to manufacture valuable compounds ranging from medicines and food ingredients to biofuels and industrial chemicals. However, turning microbes into efficient production platforms requires extensive strain optimization. Finding the right genetic changes to transform an ordinary microbe into a high-performing producer remains a major challenge, as beneficial genetic targets and gene combinations are often hidden within complex cellular networks.

phys-org.title: New mechanism shows how plants rapidly adapt to intense sunlight
phys-org.description: Plants do not wait hours to respond to intense sunlight—they react within minutes. Researchers at Bielefeld University and the Australian National University have discovered a new signaling pathway that enables plants to directly adjust their protein production before genes in the cell nucleus change their activity. The findings open new perspectives for climate-resilient crops.

phys-org.title: Evolutionary history shapes plant carbon storage strategies worldwide
phys-org.description: Two types of carbohydrates are important to plants—structural carbohydrates (which form cell walls) and nonstructural carbohydrates (NSCs). The latter group represents plants' stored energy reserves, which can be used to survive cold or drought; regrow after damage; recover from insects and disease; produce new leaves; and flower and reproduce.

phys-org.title: Researchers develop harder, longer-lasting silver plating
phys-org.description: A research team led by Seil Kim of the Korea Institute of Materials Science (KIMS) Energy & Environmental Materials Research Division has developed an Ag–PTFE composite plating technology that produces silver coatings with greater hardness and wear resistance than conventional silver plating by stably dispersing PTFE nanoparticles in a cyanide-free acidic silver plating bath.

phys-org.title: Moderate heat is enough to trigger signs of inflammation and coagulation in dairy cows
phys-org.description: Climate change is transforming livestock farming—and at a faster rate than many anticipate. More frequent and intense heat waves place a heavy physiological strain on dairy cows.

phys-org.title: AI helps scientists improve prediction of which DNA sequences bind to each other
phys-org.description: Researchers have demonstrated a novel AI model that can predict which DNA molecules bind with other DNA molecules. A more thorough understanding of these hypercomplex binding relationships has utility in applications ranging from biomedical diagnostic tools to DNA computing.

phys-org.title: Ancient Roman farm women made wine, oil and profits. Historians dismissed them as 'housekeepers'
phys-org.description: Female farm managers are hidden in plain sight in ancient Roman texts, mentioned in laws, literature and grave inscriptions across five centuries. Modern historians have generally assumed they were housekeepers, in charge of domestic tasks and household meals, and segregated from the productive business of the farm.

phys-org.title: Femcels feel doomed to loneliness
phys-org.description: Women who identify as involuntary celibates have high levels of sexual anxiety and depression, a new study suggests. The term "incel"—for involuntarily celibate—is most often associated with men, but some women describe a similar experience in online forums, where they use their own codes to express their distress. Female incels, or "femcels," feel romantically doomed by society's perception of their bodies.

phys-org.title: Ticking time bomb? Europe's aging population brings challenges

phys-org.title: Why we may still be choosing our friends like it's the Stone Age

phys-org.title: World-first neutron lens brings sharp focus to structures inside materials and objects
phys-org.description: Researchers at Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) have developed the world's first achromatic lens for neutron imaging. The lens overcomes a longstanding obstacle in the field: focusing neutrons of different wavelengths well enough to form a sharp, magnified image. With the lens, researchers can now image thick samples and follow processes inside bulky equipment such as furnaces, cryostats or pressure cells.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

proj-syn.title: Asia’s Real Energy Test
proj-syn.description: The Iran war has underscored the fragility of global energy markets, exposing which economies can withstand repeated shocks and which cannot. For ASEAN+3 countries, resilience will depend on stronger electricity systems, regional cooperation, and institutions that can manage persistent uncertainty.

proj-syn.title: The US Economy Cannot Grow Without Renewables
proj-syn.description: Consumption demand, which has long powered America’s formidable economy, rests on the promise of cheap energy. But the Trump administration has conflated that with fossil fuels, confusing historic correlation with causation and, in the process, jeopardizing long-term prosperity.

proj-syn.title: The Purpose of Development Cooperation Is to Be Unnecessary
proj-syn.description: The original promise of development cooperation was to help countries overcome poverty, build productive economies, and reduce their dependence on external resources. That has not happened, and ongoing reviews of development cooperation, which focus on donor countries' needs and priorities, are unlikely to change this.

proj-syn.title: Oil Shocks Are No Longer So Shocking
proj-syn.description: Despite this year's US/Israeli-Iran war causing the largest-ever disruption to global oil supplies, the shocks of the 1970s had a greater impact. Because oil has been used as a weapon for so long, markets, policymakers, and strategists have adapted.

proj-syn.title: The Mother of All Economic Shocks Is Chinese Mercantilism
proj-syn.description: Because analysts tend to put the United States at the center of the global economic story, they have overlooked the single most important force of the past 50 years. But it will be obvious to later generations that Chinese mercantilism has been more globally consequential than any other economic shock or policy choice.

proj-syn.title: Letting Russia Burn
proj-syn.description: From relentless Ukrainian drone strikes to soaring inflation and fuel shortages, Russia is paying an ever-higher price for Vladimir Putin's war of choice. But the war has become the organizing principle of Putin’s regime, leaving no path to lasting peace without a fundamental political transformation.

proj-syn.title: What AI Governance Demands
proj-syn.description: AI governance must account for everything from the technology’s material requirements to its effects on communities, businesses, labor markets, the environment, and strategic competition. To this end, a framework of verification-based trust—broader than national regulation and more flexible than a classic treaty—is essential.

proj-syn.title: A Japanese Wake-Up Call for America
proj-syn.description: Japan’s deepening currency and bond-market woes should be a wake-up call for other countries that appear to be on unsustainable fiscal paths, not least the United States, as well as France, Italy, and the United Kingdom. After all, a crisis in one country often draws investors' attention to others facing similar problems.

proj-syn.title: The Israel-Lebanon Recipe for Never-Ending War
proj-syn.description: Lebanon’s political circumstances, together with Iran’s strengthened regional position, make Hezbollah’s complete disarmament highly unlikely. By conditioning Israel’s withdrawal from Lebanon on this outcome—but with no provisions about cutting Hezbollah’s Iranian lifeline—the new framework agreement is dead on arrival.

proj-syn.title: Why This Energy Shock Is Different
proj-syn.description: Unlike recent energy crises, today’s geopolitical shock is destroying supply rather than rerouting it, exposing the limits of the standard policy toolkit. Governments can mitigate its impact on those most exposed, but only if fiscal and monetary policy work in concert.

proj-syn.title: China’s Erasure of Tibet Is Accelerating
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the international community has stood idly by while China has systematically eradicated Tibetan culture and identity. With the authorities stepping up their assimilation efforts, Asia risks not only losing one of its oldest civilizations, but also facing a China that is bigger, bolder, and more powerful than ever.

proj-syn.title: Judging the Enhanced Games
proj-syn.description: If fairness in sports required a level playing field that all who wish to compete could afford, that would be a reason for banning expensive performance-enhancing drugs. But it would be a reason for banning expensive high-tech swimming suits and expensive high-tech running shoes, too.

proj-syn.title: What Is the Digital-Money Debate Really About?
proj-syn.description: Both the US and Europe are moving to create digital money, but neither has the right idea about how to do it. The key is to allow “narrow banks,” which issue money but not credit, to keep their reserves in central banks and provide capped interest payments to coin holders.

proj-syn.title: An Athenian View of American Democracy
proj-syn.description: At 250, America is now producing a mindless, raw power and exponentially growing instability. The possibility of catharsis that characterized the United States at its bicentennial is hard to envisage a half-century later—to the detriment of us all.

proj-syn.title: Low-Cost Solutions to Maternal Mortality Already Exist
proj-syn.description: As foreign aid declines, policymakers in lower-income countries must increasingly focus on making better use of scarce resources. When it comes to maternal mortality, that means investing in simple, proven, and affordable interventions for postpartum hemorrhage, pre-eclampsia, and obstructed labor.

proj-syn.title: Postmodern Economics
proj-syn.description: Eschewing the idea of a single truth, the recently deceased English artist David Hockney showed that the world unfolds before us in ways we cannot fully understand. After long clinging to the pretense of certainty, economists would do well to embrace the same insight.

proj-syn.title: Digital Public Infrastructure Is Now a Strategic Battleground
proj-syn.description: Digital identity platforms, payment systems, and data exchanges promise more efficient, inclusive, and responsive public services. But in an era of geopolitical rivalry and concentrated digital power, those same systems create strategic dependencies that governments can no longer afford to ignore.

proj-syn.title: Should the Bank of Japan Raise Interest Rates?
proj-syn.description: At the beginning of 2013, when "Abenomics" was rolled out in Japan, the yen was significantly overvalued, and looser monetary policy was badly needed. Today, the opposite is true, indicating that interest-rate hikes may well be the right prescription for Japan.
